issue_context.title: TypeScript identifier resolver incorrectly handles block scopes
comments:
I don't understand what you mean by "those are the same", can you elaborate?

Type definitions in TypeScript are block-scoped. For example:

foo.ts:
```typescript
{
  interface Foo {}
}

let foo: Foo;
```

```shell
$ tsc --noEmit foo.ts
foo.ts:5:8 - error TS2304: Cannot find name 'Foo'.

5 let foo: Foo;
           ~~~
Found 1 error in foo.ts:5
```

I believe this should be treated the same as other definitions so that each interface declaration gets its own `ctxt`, similarly to [class declarations](https://play.swc.rs/?version=1.3.74&code=H4sIAAAAAAAAA6vmUgCC5JzE4mIFt%2Fx8heparlourmosogAaZax7KgAAAA%3D%3D&config=H4sIAAAAAAAAA1VPOw7DIAzdOQXy3KFi6NA79BCIOhERAYQdqSjK3QsJpM1mv4%2Ff8yqkhIkMPOVaxrJEnQjTuReEsmf9KQhwjkgm2chw6yxTpQbtCHdoOxhgnUbk6kJSd6WaA1wIhN3RsNl6O%2BT%2FTBPmmJDoKqxS7UeH10TRUmEO72Un2y%2B179HgAT9RDzsPg6VXd3JaUGxfBMLf3xcBAAA%3D) and [variable declarations](https://play.swc.rs/?version=1.3.74&code=H4sIAAAAAAAAA6vmUgCCnNQSBbf8fCuF4pKizLx0rlourmrsEgAB7XM3MAAAAA%3D%3D&config=H4sIAAAAAAAAA1VPOw7DIAzdOQXy3KFi6NA79BCIOhERAYQdqSjK3QsJpM1mv4%2Ff8yqkhIkMPOVaxrJEnQjTuReEsmf9KQhwjkgm2chw6yxTpQbtCHdoOxhgnUbk6kJSd6WaA1wIhN3RsNl6O%2BT%2FTBPmmJDoKqxS7UeH10TRUmEO72Un2y%2B179HgAT9RDzsPg6VXd3JaUGxfBMLf3xcBAAA%3D), since the scoping rules are the same. 

The `swc_ecma_ast::Ident` docs show a very similar example using variable declarations, which is being handled correctly: https://github.com/swc-project/swc/blob/e7493283120721499751f83d3753f5a3b523a1a3/crates/swc_ecma_ast/src/ident.rs#L72-L78
Why should interface declarations be treated differently?
Ping @kdy1, I'm very confused why this was closed. Can you elaborate on my questions above? I'm happy to contribute the change if you agree with my reasoning.
This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for a month. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.
